snp4.9:1.1:
[Māgandiya, a brahman, offers his daughter to the Buddha, who replies:]
“On seeing [the daughters of Māra]
—Discontent, Craving, & Passion—
snp4.9:1.2: there wasn’t even the desire for sex.
snp4.9:1.3:
So what would I want with this,
filled with urine & excrement?
snp4.9:1.4:
I wouldn’t want to touch it
even with my foot.”
snp4.9:2.1:
Māgandiya:
“If you don’t want
this gem of a woman,
snp4.9:2.3:
then for what sort of viewpoint,
habit, practice,
snp4.9:3.1:
attainment of [further] becoming
do you argue?”
snp4.9:3.3:
“‘I argue for this’
doesn’t occur to one
when considering what’s grasped
among doctrines.
snp4.9:3.4:
Looking for what is ungrasped
with regard to views,
snp4.9:3.5:
and detecting inner peace,
I saw.”
snp4.9:4.1:
Māgandiya:
“Sage, you speak
of not grasping
at any theorized judgments.
snp4.9:4.5:
How is it,
by the enlightened,
proclaimed?”
snp4.9:5.1:
The Buddha:
“He doesn’t speak of purity
in connection with view,
snp4.9:5.4:
Nor is it found by a person
through lack of view,
of learning,
snp4.9:5.5:
of knowledge,
of habit or practice.
snp4.9:5.7:
at peace,
independent,
one wouldn’t long for becoming.”
snp4.9:6.1:
Māgandiya:
“Well, if he doesn’t speak of purity
in connection with view,
snp4.9:6.4:
and it isn’t found by a person
through lack of view,
of learning,
snp4.9:6.5:
of knowledge,
of habit or practice,
snp4.9:6.6:
it seems to me that this teaching’s
simply confused,
snp4.9:6.7:
for some assume a purity
in terms of
—by means of—
a view.”
snp4.9:7.1:
The Buddha:
“Asking questions
dependent on view,
snp4.9:7.3:
you’re confused
by the things you have grasped.
snp4.9:7.4:
And so you don’t glimpse
even
the slightest
notion
snp4.9:8.1:
That’s why you think
it’s confused.
Whoever supposes
‘equal,’
‘superior,’ or
‘inferior,’
snp4.9:8.3:
whereas to one unaffected
by these three,
snp4.9:9.1: Of what would the brahman say ‘true’
snp4.9:9.2:
or ‘false,’
with whom would he dispute?
With whom would he join in dispute,
snp4.9:10.1:
Having abandoned home,
living free from society,
snp4.9:10.2:
the sage
in villages
creates no intimacies.
snp4.9:11.2:
Those things
aloof from which
he should go about in the world:
The Nāga
wouldn’t take them up
& argue for them.
snp4.9:11.5:
so the sage,
an exponent of peace,
without greed,
snp4.9:11.6:
is unsmeared by sensuality &
the world.
snp4.9:12.1:
An attainer-of-knowledge isn’t measured
made proud
snp4.9:12.4:
doesn’t reach a conclusion
in any entrenchments.
snp4.9:13.1:
For one dispassionate toward perception
there are no snares;
snp4.9:13.3: Those who grasp at perceptions & views
snp4.9:13.4: go about clashing in the world.”
